part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus went up boldly, and sat down before Kerkuon at the board; and he ate his fill of the sheep’s flesh, and drank his fill of the wine; and Theseus ate enough for three men, but Kerkuon ate enough for seven.

translation.en: Theseus stepped up boldly and sat across from Kerkuon at the table.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 담대하게 나아가 탁자에 앉아 케르키온과 마주 보았습니다.

translation.en: He ate his fill of mutton and drank plenty of wine.
translation.kr: 그는 양고기를 실컷 먹고 포도주도 양껏 마셨습니다.

translation.en: Theseus ate enough for three men, but Kerkuon ate enough for seven.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 장정 세 명의 몫을 먹어치웠으나, 케르키온은 일곱 명의 몫을 먹었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But neither spoke a word to the other, though they looked across the table by stealth; and each said in his heart, ‘He has broad shoulders; but I trust mine are as broad as his.’

translation.en: Neither spoke a word, though they stole glances at each other across the table.
translation.kr: 두 사람은 탁자 너머로 서로를 훔쳐보면서도 아무 말도 하지 않았습니다.

translation.en: Each man thought to himself, He has broad shoulders, but mine are just as broad.
translation.kr: 각자 마음속으로 저 자의 어깨가 떡 벌어지긴 했지만 내 어깨도 저만큼은 넓지라고 생각했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: At last, when the sheep was eaten and the jar of wine drained dry, King Kerkuon rose, and cried, ‘Let us wrestle a fall before we sleep.’

translation.en: Finally, when the meat was gone and the wine jar empty, King Kerkuon stood up.
translation.kr: 마침내 양고기가 다 떨어지고 포도주 항아리마저 바닥을 드러내자 케르키온 왕이 자리에서 일어났습니다.

translation.en: Let us wrestle a match before we sleep, he shouted.
translation.kr: 잠들기 전에 레슬링으로 승부를 가려보자꾸나 하고 그가 소리쳤습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: So they tossed off all their garments, and went forth in the palace-yard; and Kerkuon bade strew fresh sand in an open space between the bones.

translation.en: They tossed off their clothes and went out into the courtyard.
translation.kr: 두 사람은 옷을 훌렁 벗어 던지고 궁전 안뜰로 나갔습니다.

translation.en: Kerkuon ordered fresh sand to be scattered in an open space among the scattered bones.
translation.kr: 케르키온은 뼈들이 흩어진 공터에 깨끗한 모래를 깔라고 명령했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And there the heroes stood face to face, while their eyes glared like wild bulls’; and all the people crowded at the gates to see what would befall.

translation.en: The two men stood face to face, their eyes glaring like wild bulls.
translation.kr: 두 사내는 야생 황소처럼 눈을 부라리며 서로 마주 섰습니다.

translation.en: All the people crowded around the gates to see what would happen.
translation.kr: 모든 사람들이 무슨 일이 벌어질지 보려고 성문 주변으로 몰려들었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And there they stood and wrestled, till the stars shone out above their heads; up and down and round, till the sand was stamped hard beneath their feet.  And their eyes flashed like stars in the darkness, and their breath went up like smoke in the night air; but neither took nor gave a footstep, and the people watched silent at the gates.

translation.en: They stood and wrestled until the stars appeared above them.
translation.kr: 그들은 머리 위로 별이 뜰 때까지 서서 레슬링을 했습니다.

translation.en: They struggled up and down, stamping the sand hard beneath their feet.
translation.kr: 두 사람은 이리저리 뒤엉키며 모래바닥이 단단하게 다져지도록 짓밟았습니다.

translation.en: Their eyes flashed in the darkness, and their breath rose like smoke in the night air.
translation.kr: 어둠 속에서 그들의 두 눈은 번뜩였고 내뿜는 숨결은 밤공기에 연기처럼 피어올랐습니다.

translation.en: Neither man gave an inch, and the crowd watched in silence.
translation.kr: 두 사람 모두 한 치의 양보도 없었고 군중은 숨을 죽인 채 지켜보았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But at last Kerkuon grew angry, and caught Theseus round the neck, and shook him as a mastiff shakes a rat; but he could not shake him off his feet.

translation.en: At last Kerkuon grew angry and caught Theseus around the neck.
translation.kr: 마침내 화가 치밀어 오른 케르키온이 테세우스의 목을 부여잡았습니다.

translation.en: He shook him like a dog shakes a rat, but he could not knock him off his feet.
translation.kr: 그는 개가 쥐를 흔들듯 그를 마구 흔들어 댔지만 테세우스를 쓰러뜨리지는 못했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But Theseus was quick and wary, and clasped Kerkuon round the waist, and slipped his loin quickly underneath him, while he caught him by the wrist; and then he hove a mighty heave, a heave which would have stirred an oak, and lifted Kerkuon, and pitched him right over his shoulder on the ground.

translation.en: Theseus was quick and cautious.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 재빠르고 신중했습니다.

translation.en: He grabbed Kerkuon around the waist and quickly slipped beneath him.
translation.kr: 그는 케르키온의 허리를 끌어안고는 잽싸게 그의 몸통 밑으로 파고들었습니다.

translation.en: Catching the king by the wrist, he delivered a mighty heave that could uproot an oak.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 왕의 손목을 낚아채고 떡갈나무라도 뽑아버릴 듯한 괴력으로 밀어올렸습니다.

translation.en: He lifted Kerkuon and pitched him right over his shoulder onto the ground.
translation.kr: 그는 케르키온을 번쩍 들어 자신의 어깨 너머로 바닥에 내동댕이쳤습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then he leapt on him, and called, ‘Yield, or I kill thee!’ but Kerkuon said no word; for his heart was burst within him with the fall, and the meat, and the wine.

translation.en: Theseus leaped onto him and yelled, Yield, or I will kill you!
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그 위로 올라타서 항복하라, 그렇지 않으면 목숨을 끊겠다고 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: But Kerkuon said nothing, for his heart had burst from the heavy fall, the meat, and the wine.
translation.kr: 하지만 케르키온은 아무 대답이 없었는데, 엄청난 충격과 잔뜩 먹어댄 고기와 포도주 때문에 심장이 터져버렸기 때문입니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus opened the gates, and called in all the people; and they cried, ‘You have slain our evil king; be you now our king, and rule us well.’

translation.en: Theseus opened the gates and called all the people inside.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 성문을 열고 백성들을 모두 안으로 불러 모았습니다.

translation.en: You have killed our evil king, they cried.
translation.kr: 당신이 우리의 사악한 왕을 물리쳤소 하고 그들이 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Please be our king now and rule us well.
translation.kr: 이제 우리의 왕이 되어 우리를 잘 다스려 주십시오.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘I will be your king in Eleusis, and I will rule you right and well; for this cause I have slain all evil-doers—Sinis, and Sciron, and this man last of all.’

translation.en: I will be your king in Eleusis, and I will rule you justly.
translation.kr: 내가 엘레우시스에서 여러분의 왕이 되어 공정하게 다스리겠습니다.

translation.en: This is why I have slain all these evildoers, Sinis, Sciron, and finally this man.
translation.kr: 시니스와 스키론, 그리고 마침내 이 자까지 사악한 무리들을 모두 처단한 것도 바로 그 때문입니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then an aged man stepped forth, and said, ‘Young hero, hast thou slain Sinis?  Beware then of Ægeus, king of Athens, to whom thou goest, for he is near of kin to Sinis.’

translation.en: Then an old man stepped forward.
translation.kr: 그때 한 노인이 앞으로 나섰습니다.

translation.en: Young hero, have you killed Sinis? he asked.
translation.kr: 젊은 영웅이여, 시니스를 물리쳤단 말이오? 하고 그가 물었습니다.

translation.en: Beware of Aegeus, the king of Athens, to whom you travel.
translation.kr: 당신이 찾아가려는 아테네의 왕 아이게우스를 조심하시오.

translation.en: He is a close relative of Sinis.
translation.kr: 그는 시니스와 가까운 친척이라오.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Then I have slain my own kinsman,’ said Theseus, ‘though well he deserved to die.  Who will purge me from his death, for rightfully I slew him, unrighteous and accursed as he was?’

translation.en: Then I have killed my own relative, Theseus said, though he certainly deserved to die.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 내 핏줄을 내 손으로 죽였단 말이군 하고 테세우스가 말하길, 비록 그가 죽어 마땅한 자이긴 했지만 말이오 했습니다.

translation.en: Who will purify me of his blood?
translation.kr: 누가 이 피의 죄악을 씻어 주겠소?

translation.en: I killed him rightfully, for he was wicked and cursed.
translation.kr: 그는 사악하고 저주받은 자였기에 나는 정당하게 그를 물리쳤단 말이오.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And the old man answered—

translation.en: The old man replied.
translation.kr: 노인이 대답했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘That will the heroes do, the sons of Phytalus, who dwell beneath the elm-tree in Aphidnai, by the bank of silver Cephisus; for they know the mysteries of the Gods.  Thither you shall go and be purified, and after you shall be our king.’

translation.en: The heroes will do that.
translation.kr: 그 일은 영웅들이 해 줄 것이오.

translation.en: They are the sons of Phytalus, who live beneath the elm tree in Aphidnai by the silver Cephisus river.
translation.kr: 그들은 은빛 케피수스 강변 아피드나이의 느릅나무 아래에 사는 피탈로스의 아들들이라오.

translation.en: They know the mysteries of the gods.
translation.kr: 그들은 신들의 신비로운 의식을 잘 알고 있지요.

translation.en: You must go there to be purified, and afterward you shall be our king.
translation.kr: 그곳으로 가서 정화 의식을 치른 뒤에 돌아와 우리의 왕이 되어 주시오.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: So he took an oath of the people of Eleusis, that they would serve him as their king, and went away next morning across the Thriasian plain, and over the hills toward Aphidnai, that he might find the sons of Phytalus.

translation.en: Theseus made the people of Eleusis swear an oath to serve him as king.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 엘레우시스 백성들에게 자신을 왕으로 섬기겠다는 맹세를 받았습니다.

translation.en: The next morning, he set out across the Thriasian plain and over the hills toward Aphidnai to find the sons of Phytalus.
translation.kr: 다음 날 아침, 그는 피탈로스의 아들들을 찾기 위해 트리아시아 평원을 가로질러 언덕을 넘어 아피드나이를 향해 길을 나섰습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And as he was skirting the Vale of Cephisus, along the foot of lofty Parnes, a very tall and strong man came down to meet him, dressed in rich garments.  On his arms were golden bracelets, and round his neck a collar of jewels; and he came forward, bowing courteously, and held out both his hands, and spoke—

translation.en: As he skirted the edge of the valley along the foot of Mount Parnes, a tall, strong man approached him.
translation.kr: 그가 우뚝 솟은 파르네스 산기슭을 따라 계곡 가장자리를 돌고 있을 때, 키가 크고 건장한 남자가 다가왔습니다.

translation.en: He was dressed in rich clothes, wearing golden bracelets and a jeweled collar.
translation.kr: 그는 값비싼 옷을 입고 양팔에는 금팔찌를 두르고 목에는 보석 목걸이를 걸고 있었습니다.

translation.en: The man came forward, bowing politely, held out his hands, and spoke.
translation.kr: 남자는 앞으로 다가와 정중하게 고개 숙여 인사하고는 두 손을 내밀며 말했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Welcome, fair youth, to these mountains; happy am I to have met you! For what greater pleasure to a good man, than to entertain strangers? But I see that you are weary.  Come up to my castle, and rest yourself awhile.’

translation.en: Welcome to these mountains, young man. I am happy to meet you!
translation.kr: 이 깊은 산속에 오신 것을 환영하오 젊은이. 만나게 되어 참으로 기쁘구려!

translation.en: What greater pleasure is there for a good man than to entertain strangers?
translation.kr: 선한 사람에게 낯선 나그네를 대접하는 것보다 더 큰 기쁨이 어디 있겠소?

translation.en: I can see that you are tired.
translation.kr: 보아하니 몹시 지친 것 같소만.

translation.en: Come up to my castle and rest for a while.
translation.kr: 내 성으로 올라가서 잠시 쉬어 가시지요.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘I give you thanks,’ said Theseus: ‘but I am in haste to go up the valley, and to reach Aphidnai in the Vale of Cephisus.’

translation.en: Thank you, Theseus replied, but I am in a hurry.
translation.kr: 감사합니다 하고 테세우스가 답하길, 하지만 저는 갈 길이 바쁩니다 했습니다.

translation.en: I need to travel up the valley and reach Aphidnai.
translation.kr: 계곡을 따라 올라가 아피드나이에 서둘러 당도해야 하거든요.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Alas! you have wandered far from the right way, and you cannot reach Aphidnai to-night, for there are many miles of mountain between you and it, and steep passes, and cliffs dangerous after nightfall.  It is well for you that I met you, for my whole joy is to find strangers, and to feast them at my castle, and hear tales from them of foreign lands.  Come up with me, and eat the best of venison, and drink the rich red wine, and sleep upon my famous bed, of which all travellers say that they never saw the like.  For whatsoever the stature of my guest, however tall or short, that bed fits him to a hair, and he sleeps on it as he never slept before.’  And he laid hold on Theseus’ hands, and would not let him go.

translation.en: Alas! You have wandered far from the right path.
translation.kr: 이런! 길을 단단히 잘못 드셨구려.

translation.en: You cannot reach Aphidnai tonight, for miles of steep passes and dangerous cliffs lie ahead.
translation.kr: 가파른 고갯길과 위험한 절벽이 까마득히 이어져 있어 오늘 밤엔 아피드나이에 절대 닿지 못할 거요.

translation.en: It is a good thing I found you, for my greatest joy is feasting strangers in my castle and hearing their tales.
translation.kr: 나를 만난 게 참으로 다행이지 않소. 낯선 사람들을 성으로 데려가 잔치를 베풀고 그들의 모험담을 듣는 것이 내 유일한 낙이라오.

translation.en: Come with me to eat the best venison and drink rich red wine.
translation.kr: 나와 함께 가서 최고급 사슴고기를 맛보고 향긋한 붉은 포도주도 마시도록 합시다.

translation.en: You can sleep upon my famous bed, which travelers say is unlike any other.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 여행자들 사이에서 칭송이 자자한 내 특별한 침대에 누워 푹 쉬시구려.

translation.en: Whether a guest is tall or short, the bed fits him perfectly, giving him the best sleep of his life.
translation.kr: 키가 크든 작든 손님의 체격에 머리카락 하나 안 틀리고 딱 맞춘 듯해서 평생 처음 겪는 달콤한 잠을 선사한다오.

translation.en: The man grabbed Theseus by the hands and would not let him go.
translation.kr: 남자는 테세우스의 손을 부여잡고는 결코 놓아주려 하지 않았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Theseus wished to go forwards: but he was ashamed to seem churlish to so hospitable a man; and he was curious to see that wondrous bed; and beside, he was hungry and weary: yet he shrank from the man, he knew not why; for, though his voice was gentle and fawning, it was dry and husky like a toad’s; and though his eyes were gentle, they were dull and cold like stones.  But he consented, and went with the man up a glen which led from the road toward the peaks of Parnes, under the dark shadow of the cliffs.

translation.en: Theseus wanted to keep moving, but he felt bad refusing such a welcoming host.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 계속 길을 재촉하고 싶었지만 이렇게 환대해 주는 사람에게 무례하게 굴기가 미안했습니다.

translation.en: He was also hungry, tired, and curious to see this wondrous bed.
translation.kr: 게다가 배도 고프고 몹시 지쳐 있던 터라 그 신기한 침대를 한번 보고 싶은 호기심도 생겼습니다.

translation.en: Still, something about the man made him hesitate.
translation.kr: 그럼에도 웬일인지 그 남자에게서 묘한 거부감이 느껴졌습니다.

translation.en: His voice was gentle but dry and husky like a toad, and his eyes were dull and cold as stone.
translation.kr: 그의 목소리는 부드럽고 상냥했지만 두꺼비처럼 건조하고 쇳소리가 났으며, 눈빛 또한 친절해 보이면서도 돌멩이처럼 탁하고 차가웠기 때문입니다.

translation.en: Finally, Theseus agreed and followed the man up a narrow valley toward the dark cliffs of Mount Parnes.
translation.kr: 결국 테세우스는 그를 따라 굽이진 길을 지나 파르네스의 산봉우리를 향해 드리워진 짙은 절벽 그림자 아래 좁은 골짜기로 들어섰습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And as they went up, the glen grew narrower, and the cliffs higher and darker, and beneath them a torrent roared, half seen between bare limestone crags.  And around there was neither tree nor bush, while from the white peaks of Parnes the snow-blasts swept down the glen, cutting and chilling till a horror fell on Theseus as he looked round at that doleful place.  And he asked at last, ‘Your castle stands, it seems, in a dreary region.’

translation.en: As they climbed, the valley grew narrower, and the cliffs loomed higher and darker.
translation.kr: 위로 올라갈수록 골짜기는 더욱 좁아지고 절벽은 한층 더 높고 어두컴컴해졌습니다.

translation.en: A roaring torrent flowed far below them through the bare limestone rocks.
translation.kr: 저 아래 앙상한 석회암 바위들 틈새로는 세찬 급류가 소리치며 흐르고 있었습니다.

translation.en: There were no trees or bushes, and freezing wind swept down from the snowy peaks.
translation.kr: 주변엔 나무 한 그루, 덤불 하나 찾아볼 수 없었고 하얗게 눈 덮인 산봉우리에서 불어온 매서운 눈보라가 골짜기를 할퀴듯 몰아쳤습니다.

translation.en: A sense of dread fell upon Theseus as he looked around the gloomy place.
translation.kr: 그 을씨년스러운 풍경을 둘러보던 테세우스의 마음에 왠지 모를 두려움이 엄습했습니다.

translation.en: He finally said, It seems your castle stands in a rather dreary region.
translation.kr: 결국 그가 입을 열어 댁의 성은 다소 음산한 곳에 자리 잡고 있군요 하고 말했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Yes; but once within it, hospitality makes all things cheerful.  But who are these?’ and he looked back, and Theseus also; and far below, along the road which they had left, came a string of laden asses, and merchants walking by them, watching their ware.

translation.en: Yes, but once inside, my hospitality makes everything cheerful.
translation.kr: 그렇긴 하지만 일단 성에 들어서서 대접을 받다 보면 모든 게 즐거워질 거요.

translation.en: But who are these people? the man asked, looking back.
translation.kr: 아니, 저 사람들은 누굴까? 하고 남자가 뒤를 돌아보며 물었습니다.

translation.en: Theseus looked down and saw merchants leading loaded donkeys along the road below.
translation.kr: 테세우스도 뒤를 돌아 저 멀리 아래쪽 길을 내려다보니 상인들이 물건을 잔뜩 짊어진 당나귀들을 줄지어 몰고 오고 있었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Ah, poor souls!’ said the stranger.  ‘Well for them that I looked back and saw them!  And well for me too, for I shall have the more guests at my feast.  Wait awhile till I go down and call them, and we will eat and drink together the livelong night.  Happy am I, to whom Heaven sends so many guests at once!’

translation.en: Ah, the poor souls! said the stranger.
translation.kr: 아, 가엾은 사람들! 하고 남자가 말했습니다.

translation.en: It is a good thing I looked back and saw them!
translation.kr: 내가 뒤를 돌아봐서 저들을 발견했으니 참으로 다행이오!

translation.en: It is good for me too, for I will have more guests at my feast.
translation.kr: 내 잔치에 손님이 더 늘게 되었으니 나에게도 좋은 일이지요.

translation.en: Wait here while I go down and call them, so we can all eat and drink together tonight.
translation.kr: 내가 내려가 저들을 데려올 테니 여기서 잠시만 기다리시오, 그러면 밤새도록 다 함께 먹고 마실 수 있을 거요.

translation.en: I am so lucky that heaven has sent me all these guests at once!
translation.kr: 하늘이 이렇게 한꺼번에 많은 손님을 보내 주시다니 나는 정말 운이 좋은 사람이오!

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And he ran back down the hill, waving his hand and shouting, to the merchants, while Theseus went slowly up the steep pass.

translation.en: He ran back down the hill, waving his hand and shouting to the merchants.
translation.kr: 그는 언덕 아래로 달려 내려가 상인들을 향해 손을 흔들며 크게 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Meanwhile, Theseus continued slowly up the steep mountain pass.
translation.kr: 그사이 테세우스는 가파른 산길을 따라 천천히 걸어 올라갔습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But as he went up he met an aged man, who had been gathering drift-wood in the torrent-bed.  He had laid down his faggot in the road, and was trying to lift it again to his shoulder.  And when he saw Theseus, he called to him, and said—

translation.en: As he climbed, he met an old man who had been gathering firewood from the riverbed.
translation.kr: 계속 걸어 올라가던 그는 강바닥에서 땔감을 줍고 있던 한 노인과 마주쳤습니다.

translation.en: The man had set his bundle down and was struggling to lift it back onto his shoulder.
translation.kr: 노인은 장작단을 길바닥에 내려놓고 다시 어깨에 짊어지려고 몹시 쩔쩔매고 있었습니다.

translation.en: When he saw Theseus, he called out to him.
translation.kr: 테세우스를 본 그가 소리쳐 불렀습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘O fair youth, help me up with my burden, for my limbs are stiff and weak with years.’

translation.en: Young man, please help me lift my burden.
translation.kr: 젊은이, 이 짐을 올리는 것 좀 도와주구려.

translation.en: My limbs are stiff and weak with age.
translation.kr: 나이가 들어 팔다리가 뻣뻣하고 기운이 하나도 없어서 그렇소.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus lifted the burden on his back.  And the old man blest him, and then looked earnestly upon him, and said—

translation.en: Theseus lifted the burden onto his back.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 짐을 등 위로 들어 올렸습니다.

translation.en: The old man blessed him, looked earnestly at him, and spoke.
translation.kr: 노인은 그를 축복하고 진지하게 바라보며 말했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Who are you, fair youth, and wherefore travel you this doleful road?’

translation.en: Who are you, fair youth, and why do you travel this sorrowful road?
translation.kr: 아름다운 젊은이여, 당신은 누구이며 왜 이 슬픈 길을 여행하고 있습니까?

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Who I am my parents know; but I travel this doleful road because I have been invited by a hospitable man, who promises to feast me, and to make me sleep upon I know not what wondrous bed.’

translation.en: My parents know who I am.
translation.kr: 제 부모님은 제가 누구인지 알고 계십니다.

translation.en: But I travel this sad road because a hospitable man invited me.
translation.kr: 하지만 어떤 친절한 남자가 저를 초대했기 때문에 이 슬픈 길을 여행하고 있습니다.

translation.en: He promised to feast me and let me sleep on some wondrous bed.
translation.kr: 그는 저를 대접하고 어떤 놀라운 침대에서 재워주겠다고 약속했습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then the old man clapped his hands together and cried—

translation.en: The old man clapped his hands together and cried out.
translation.kr: 그러자 노인은 두 손을 마주치며 소리쳤습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘O house of Hades, man-devouring! will thy maw never be full?  Know, fair youth, that you are going to torment and to death, for he who met you (I will requite your kindness by another) is a robber and a murderer of men. Whatsoever stranger he meets he entices him hither to death; and as for this bed of which he speaks, truly it fits all comers, yet none ever rose alive off it save me.’

translation.en: Oh, man-devouring house of Hades!
translation.kr: 아, 사람을 집어삼키는 하데스의 집이여!

translation.en: Will your stomach never be full?
translation.kr: 당신의 배는 영원히 채워지지 않을 것입니까?

translation.en: Know this, fair youth, you are heading to torment and death.
translation.kr: 아름다운 젊은이여, 당신은 고통과 죽음을 향해 가고 있다는 것을 아십시오.

translation.en: I will return your kindness by warning you.
translation.kr: 당신의 친절에 보답하기 위해 경고하겠습니다.

translation.en: The man who met you is a robber and a murderer.
translation.kr: 당신이 만난 남자는 강도이자 살인마입니다.

translation.en: He entices every stranger he meets here to their death.
translation.kr: 그는 만나는 모든 낯선 사람들을 이곳으로 유인하여 죽입니다.

translation.en: As for that bed he speaks of, it truly fits all comers.
translation.kr: 그가 말하는 그 침대는 모든 방문객에게 딱 맞습니다.

translation.en: Yet no one has ever risen alive from it except me.
translation.kr: 하지만 나를 제외하고는 아무도 그곳에서 살아서 일어난 적이 없습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Why?’ asked Theseus, astonished.

translation.en: Why? asked Theseus, astonished.
translation.kr: 왜입니까? 테세우스가 깜짝 놀라 물었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Because, if a man be too tall for it, he lops his limbs till they be short enough, and if he be too short, he stretches his limbs till they be long enough: but me only he spared, seven weary years agone; for I alone of all fitted his bed exactly, so he spared me, and made me his slave. And once I was a wealthy merchant, and dwelt in brazen-gated Thebes; but now I hew wood and draw water for him, the torment of all mortal men.’

translation.en: If a man is too tall for it, he chops off his limbs until they are short enough.
translation.kr: 만약 사람이 너무 크면 그는 다리가 짧아질 때까지 잘라냅니다.

translation.en: If he is too short, he stretches his limbs until they are long enough.
translation.kr: 만약 너무 작으면 다리가 길어질 때까지 늘립니다.

translation.en: He only spared me seven weary years ago.
translation.kr: 그는 7년 전 힘들었던 때에 나만을 살려주었습니다.

translation.en: I alone perfectly fitted his bed, so he made me his slave.
translation.kr: 나만이 유일하게 그의 침대에 딱 맞았고 그래서 그는 나를 노예로 삼았습니다.

translation.en: I was once a wealthy merchant living in brazen-gated Thebes.
translation.kr: 저는 한때 청동 문이 있는 테베에 살던 부유한 상인이었습니다.

translation.en: But now I chop wood and draw water for this tormentor of all mortal men.
translation.kr: 하지만 지금은 모든 인간을 괴롭히는 그를 위해 장작을 패고 물을 긷고 있습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus said nothing; but he ground his teeth together.

translation.en: Theseus said nothing, but he ground his teeth together.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 아무 말도 하지 않았지만 이를 갈았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Escape, then,’ said the old man, ‘for he will have no pity on thy youth. But yesterday he brought up hither a young man and a maiden, and fitted them upon his bed; and the young man’s hands and feet he cut off, but the maiden’s limbs he stretched until she died, and so both perished miserably—but I am tired of weeping over the slain.  And therefore he is called Procrustes the stretcher, though his father called him Damastes. Flee from him: yet whither will you flee?  The cliffs are steep, and who can climb them? and there is no other road.’

translation.en: Escape, then, said the old man.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 도망치십시오, 노인이 말했습니다.

translation.en: He will have no pity on your youth.
translation.kr: 그는 당신의 젊음을 불쌍히 여기지 않을 것입니다.

translation.en: Just yesterday he brought a young man and a maiden here.
translation.kr: 바로 어제 그는 젊은 남자와 처녀를 이곳으로 데려왔습니다.

translation.en: He fitted them upon his bed.
translation.kr: 그는 그들을 침대에 맞추었습니다.

translation.en: He cut off the young man's hands and feet.
translation.kr: 그는 젊은 남자의 손과 발을 잘랐습니다.

translation.en: He stretched the maiden's limbs until she died.
translation.kr: 그는 처녀가 죽을 때까지 팔다리를 늘렸습니다.

translation.en: So both perished miserably.
translation.kr: 그래서 두 사람 모두 비참하게 죽고 말았습니다.

translation.en: I am so tired of weeping over the slain.
translation.kr: 살해당한 사람들을 위해 우는 것도 이제 지쳤습니다.

translation.en: That is why he is called Procrustes the stretcher.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 늘리는 자 프로크루스테스라고 불립니다.

translation.en: His father originally named him Damastes.
translation.kr: 그의 아버지는 원래 그를 다마스테스라고 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Flee from him, yet where will you go?
translation.kr: 그에게서 도망치십시오, 하지만 어디로 가시겠습니까?

translation.en: The cliffs are steep, and no one can climb them.
translation.kr: 절벽은 가파르고 아무도 오를 수 없습니다.

translation.en: There is no other road.
translation.kr: 다른 길은 없습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But Theseus laid his hand upon the old man’s month, and said, ‘There is no need to flee;’ and he turned to go down the pass.

translation.en: But Theseus covered the old man's mouth with his hand.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 노인의 입을 손으로 막았습니다.

translation.en: There is no need to flee, he said.
translation.kr: 도망칠 필요가 없습니다, 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: He then turned to head down the pass.
translation.kr: 그러고는 고개를 돌려 길을 따라 내려갔습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Do not tell him that I have warned you, or he will kill me by some evil death;’ and the old man screamed after him down the glen; but Theseus strode on in his wrath.

translation.en: Do not tell him that I have warned you, or he will kill me brutally!
translation.kr: 제가 경고했다고 그에게 말하지 마십시오, 아니면 저를 잔인하게 죽일 것입니다!

translation.en: The old man screamed after him down the glen.
translation.kr: 노인은 계곡 아래로 가는 그를 향해 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus strode on in his wrath.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 분노에 차 성큼성큼 걸어갔습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And he said to himself, ‘This is an ill-ruled land; when shall I have done ridding it of monsters?’  And as he spoke, Procrustes came up the hill, and all the merchants with him, smiling and talking gaily.  And when he saw Theseus, he cried, ‘Ah, fair young guest, have I kept you too long waiting?’

translation.en: He said to himself, this is a poorly ruled land.
translation.kr: 그는 속으로 이 땅은 통치가 엉망이라고 생각했습니다.

translation.en: When will I finish ridding it of monsters?
translation.kr: 언제쯤 이 괴물들을 다 없앨 수 있을까?

translation.en: As he spoke, Procrustes came up the hill.
translation.kr: 그가 말할 때 프로크루스테스가 언덕을 올라왔습니다.

translation.en: He had merchants with him, all smiling and chatting happily.
translation.kr: 그는 상인들과 함께 모두 웃으며 즐겁게 이야기하고 있었습니다.

translation.en: When he saw Theseus, he cried out.
translation.kr: 그는 테세우스를 보자마자 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Ah, fair young guest, have I kept you waiting too long?
translation.kr: 아, 아름다운 젊은 손님이여, 제가 너무 오래 기다리게 했습니까?

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: But Theseus answered, ‘The man who stretches his guests upon a bed and hews off their hands and feet, what shall be done to him, when right is done throughout the land?’

translation.en: But Theseus answered him directly.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 그에게 단도직입적으로 대답했습니다.

translation.en: When justice rules the land, what should be done to a man like you?
translation.kr: 정의가 온 땅을 지배할 때 당신 같은 사람은 어떻게 되어야 합니까?

translation.en: You stretch your guests on a bed and chop off their limbs.
translation.kr: 손님들을 침대에 눕혀 팔다리를 잘라버리는 자 말입니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Procrustes’ countenance changed, and his cheeks grew as green as a lizard, and he felt for his sword in haste; but Theseus leapt on him, and cried—

translation.en: Procrustes' expression immediately changed.
translation.kr: 프로크루스테스의 표정이 즉시 바뀌었습니다.

translation.en: His cheeks turned as green as a lizard.
translation.kr: 그의 뺨은 도마뱀처럼 초록색으로 변했습니다.

translation.en: He hastily reached for his sword.
translation.kr: 그는 서둘러 칼을 찾았습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus leaped onto him and shouted.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 그에게 달려들며 소리쳤습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Is this true, my host, or is it false?’ and he clasped Procrustes round waist and elbow, so that he could not draw his sword.

translation.en: Is this true, my host, or is it false?
translation.kr: 이것이 사실입니까, 나의 주인이여, 아니면 거짓입니까?

translation.en: He grabbed Procrustes tightly by the waist and elbow.
translation.kr: 그는 프로크루스테스의 허리와 팔꿈치를 단단히 붙잡았습니다.

translation.en: This trapped him so he could not draw his sword.
translation.kr: 그렇게 그를 묶어두어 칼을 뽑을 수 없게 만들었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: ‘Is this true, my host, or is it false?’  But Procrustes answered never a word.

translation.en: Is this true, my host, or is it false?
translation.kr: 이것이 사실입니까, 나의 주인이여, 아니면 거짓입니까?

translation.en: But Procrustes did not answer a single word.
translation.kr: 하지만 프로크루스테스는 단 한마디도 대답하지 않았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus flung him from him, and lifted up his dreadful club; and before Procrustes could strike him he had struck, and felled him to the ground.

translation.en: Theseus flung him away and raised his dreadful club.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그를 내동댕이치고 무시무시한 곤봉을 치켜들었습니다.

translation.en: Before Procrustes could strike, Theseus swung first.
translation.kr: 프로크루스테스가 공격하기도 전에 테세우스가 먼저 휘둘렀습니다.

translation.en: The blow sent him crashing to the ground.
translation.kr: 그 일격에 그는 땅에 쓰러졌습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And once again he struck him; and his evil soul fled forth, and went down to Hades squeaking, like a bat into the darkness of a cave.

translation.en: He struck him once more.
translation.kr: 그는 그를 한 번 더 때렸습니다.

translation.en: His evil soul fled from his body.
translation.kr: 그의 사악한 영혼이 몸에서 빠져나갔습니다.

translation.en: It squeaked like a bat disappearing into a dark cave.
translation.kr: 마치 어두운 동굴로 사라지는 박쥐처럼 찍찍거리며 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: Then it descended into the realm of Hades.
translation.kr: 그러고는 하데스의 영역으로 내려갔습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then Theseus stript him of his gold ornaments, and went up to his house, and found there great wealth and treasure, which he had stolen from the passers-by.  And he called the people of the country, whom Procrustes had spoiled a long time, and parted the spoil among them, and went down the mountains, and away.

translation.en: Theseus stripped him of his gold ornaments.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 그의 금 장신구를 벗겨냈습니다.

translation.en: He went up to his house and found vast wealth and treasure.
translation.kr: 그는 그의 집으로 올라가 엄청난 부와 보물을 발견했습니다.

translation.en: It had all been stolen from passing travelers.
translation.kr: 그것들은 모두 지나가는 여행객들에게서 훔친 것이었습니다.

translation.en: He summoned the local people whom Procrustes had long oppressed.
translation.kr: 그는 오랫동안 프로크루스테스에게 억압받던 지역 사람들을 불렀습니다.

translation.en: He divided the spoils among them.
translation.kr: 그는 그들에게 전리품을 나누어 주었습니다.

translation.en: Then he traveled down the mountains and moved on.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 그는 산을 내려가 길을 떠났습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And he went down the glens of Parnes, through mist, and cloud, and rain, down the slopes of oak, and lentisk, and arbutus, and fragrant bay, till he came to the Vale of Cephisus, and the pleasant town of Aphidnai, and the home of the Phytalid heroes, where they dwelt beneath a mighty elm.

translation.en: He hiked down the glens of Mount Parnes.
translation.kr: 그는 파르네스 산의 계곡을 따라 걸어 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: He passed through mist, cloud, and heavy rain.
translation.kr: 그는 안개와 구름, 그리고 쏟아지는 비를 뚫고 지나갔습니다.

translation.en: He descended slopes covered in oak, mastic, and fragrant bay trees.
translation.kr: 그는 참나무와 매스틱, 향기로운 월계수가 덮인 비탈을 내려갔습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he reached the Vale of Cephisus.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 케피소스 계곡에 도착했습니다.

translation.en: He found the pleasant town of Aphidnai.
translation.kr: 그는 아름다운 마을 아피드나이를 발견했습니다.

translation.en: There stood the home of the Phytalid heroes.
translation.kr: 그곳에는 피탈리드 영웅들의 집이 있었습니다.

translation.en: They lived peacefully beneath a massive elm tree.
translation.kr: 그들은 거대한 느릅나무 아래에서 평화롭게 살고 있었습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And there they built an altar, and bade him bathe in Cephisus, and offer a yearling ram, and purified him from the blood of Sinis, and sent him away in peace.

translation.en: The heroes built an altar for him.
translation.kr: 영웅들은 그를 위해 제단을 쌓았습니다.

translation.en: They told him to bathe in the Cephisus river.
translation.kr: 그들은 그에게 케피소스 강에서 목욕하라고 말했습니다.

translation.en: He offered a yearling ram as a sacrifice.
translation.kr: 그는 1년 된 숫양을 제물로 바쳤습니다.

translation.en: They purified him from the bloodshed of Sinis.
translation.kr: 그들은 시니스를 죽인 피에서 그를 정화해주었습니다.

translation.en: Then they sent him on his way in peace.
translation.kr: 그러고 나서 그를 평화롭게 떠나보냈습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And he went down the valley by Acharnai, and by the silver-swirling stream, while all the people blessed him, for the fame of his prowess had spread wide, till he saw the plain of Athens, and the hill where Athené dwells.

translation.en: He traveled down the valley near Acharnai.
translation.kr: 그는 아카르나이 근처의 계곡을 따라 여행했습니다.

translation.en: He walked alongside the silver-swirling stream.
translation.kr: 그는 은빛으로 소용돌이치는 냇물을 따라 걸었습니다.

translation.en: All the people blessed him along the way.
translation.kr: 모든 사람들이 길을 지나는 그를 축복했습니다.

translation.en: The fame of his incredible prowess had already spread far.
translation.kr: 그의 놀라운 용맹함에 대한 명성이 이미 멀리 퍼져 있었습니다.

translation.en: Eventually, he saw the great plain of Athens.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 거대한 아테네 평원을 보았습니다.

translation.en: He gazed upon the holy hill where Athena dwells.
translation.kr: 그는 아테나 여신이 머무는 신성한 언덕을 바라보았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: So Theseus went up through Athens, and all the people ran out to see him; for his fame had gone before him and every one knew of his mighty deeds. And all cried, ‘Here comes the hero who slew Sinis, and Phaia the wild sow of Crommyon, and conquered Kerkuon in wrestling, and slew Procrustes the pitiless.’  But Theseus went on sadly and steadfastly, for his heart yearned after his father; and he said, ‘How shall I deliver him from these leeches who suck his blood?’

translation.en: Theseus made his way up through Athens.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 아테네를 향해 걸어 올라갔습니다.

translation.en: The people ran out to see him, as his fame preceded him.
translation.kr: 그의 명성이 먼저 퍼져 사람들은 그를 보려고 달려나왔습니다.

translation.en: Everyone knew of his mighty deeds.
translation.kr: 모두가 그의 위대한 업적을 알고 있었습니다.

translation.en: They cried out, here comes the great hero!
translation.kr: 그들은 위대한 영웅이 오셨다며 소리쳤습니다!

translation.en: He slew Sinis and the wild sow of Crommyon.
translation.kr: 그는 시니스와 크로미온의 야생 암돼지를 죽였습니다.

translation.en: He defeated Kerkuon in wrestling and struck down pitiless Procrustes.
translation.kr: 그는 레슬링에서 케르키온을 물리쳤고 무자비한 프로크루스테스를 쓰러뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: But Theseus kept walking sadly and steadfastly.
translation.kr: 하지만 테세우스는 슬프고도 확고하게 계속 걸어갔습니다.

translation.en: His heart deeply yearned for his father.
translation.kr: 그의 마음은 아버지를 간절히 그리워했습니다.

translation.en: How will I save him from these leeches sucking his blood?
translation.kr: 그의 피를 빠는 거머리 같은 자들로부터 어떻게 그를 구할 수 있을까?

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: So he went up the holy stairs, and into the Acropolis, where Ægeus’ palace stood; and he went straight into Ægeus’ hall, and stood upon the threshold, and looked round.

translation.en: He climbed the holy stairs into the Acropolis.
translation.kr: 그는 신성한 계단을 올라 아크로폴리스로 들어갔습니다.

translation.en: This was where the palace of King Aegeus stood.
translation.kr: 그곳은 아이게우스 왕의 궁전이 있는 곳이었습니다.

translation.en: He walked straight into the main hall.
translation.kr: 그는 대연회장으로 곧장 걸어갔습니다.

translation.en: He stood upon the threshold and looked around.
translation.kr: 그는 문지방에 서서 주위를 둘러보았습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: And there he saw his cousins sitting about the table at the wine: many a son of Pallas, but no Ægeus among them.  There they sat and feasted, and laughed, and passed the wine-cup round; while harpers harped, and slave-girls sang, and the tumblers showed their tricks.

translation.en: He saw his cousins sitting around the table drinking wine.
translation.kr: 그는 사촌들이 탁자에 둘러앉아 포도주를 마시는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: Many sons of Pallas were present, but Aegeus was nowhere to be found.
translation.kr: 팔라스의 아들들은 많았지만 아이게우스는 어디에도 없었습니다.

translation.en: They feasted, laughed, and passed the wine cup around.
translation.kr: 그들은 포식을 하고 웃으며 포도주 잔을 돌렸습니다.

translation.en: Musicians played their harps while slave girls sang.
translation.kr: 노예 소녀들이 노래하는 동안 악사들은 하프를 연주했습니다.

translation.en: Acrobats showed off their tumbling tricks for the crowd.
translation.kr: 곡예사들은 무리를 위해 구르기 묘기를 선보였습니다.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Loud laughed the sons of Pallas, and fast went the wine-cup round; but Theseus frowned, and said under his breath, ‘No wonder that the land is full of robbers, while such as these bear rule.’

translation.en: The sons of Pallas laughed loudly.
translation.kr: 팔라스의 아들들은 크게 웃었습니다.

translation.en: The wine cup passed quickly from hand to hand.
translation.kr: 포도주 잔이 빠르게 이 손에서 저 손으로 넘어갔습니다.

translation.en: Theseus frowned and muttered under his breath.
translation.kr: 테세우스는 얼굴을 찌푸리며 낮은 목소리로 중얼거렸습니다.

translation.en: No wonder the land is full of robbers when fools like these rule.
translation.kr: 이런 바보들이 통치하니 나라에 도둑이 넘쳐나는 것도 당연하지.

part: Part II: How Theseus Slew the Devourers of Men
raw: Then the Pallantids saw him, and called to him, half-drunk with wine, ‘Holla, tall stranger at the door, what is your will to-day?’

translation.en: The sons of Pallas noticed him standing there.
translation.kr: 팔라스의 아들들은 그곳에 서 있는 그를 알아차렸습니다.

translation.en: Half-drunk with wine, they called out to him.
translation.kr: 포도주에 반쯤 취한 그들이 그에게 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Hey, tall stranger at the door, what do you want today?
translation.kr: 이봐, 문에 서 있는 키 큰 이방인, 오늘은 무슨 일로 왔나?
